mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP indicates strong economic activity, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If GDP increases but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in unemployment rate above 6% signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If unemployment exceeds 6% but S&P 500 returns remain positive.

mechanism_narrative: When both unemployment rate decreases and employment increases, it indicates a strong labor market, boosting S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If both proxies improve but S&P 500 returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: Lower federal funds rate stimulates economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS drops but S&P 500 returns are not positive.

mechanism_narrative: Higher inflation leads to tighter monetary policy, negatively impacting S&P 500 returns over 5 days.
failure_condition: If inflation rises but S&P 500 returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production indicates weaker supply chains, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If INDPRO falls below 100 but S&P 500 returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: Rising GDP and housing starts indicate strong demand, boosting S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: If both proxies rise but S&P 500 returns are negative.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion, slowing retail sales signal weaker demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If RSAFS growth slows but S&P 500 returns are positive.
